newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African rand was trading Thursday's local session in a tight, but weaker range with local players casting an eye to movements in the U.S. dollar for Friday's direction.
The local unit was last priced at 4.4675/4705 from Wednesday's late level of 4.4565/4595, having slipped early on the back of some importers searching for dollars.

"We're seeing some reasonable two-way trades but it's very quiet. I think its still in a range but it (Friday's sentiment) will depend on what the dollar does. I think the rand overall will remain stable," said one dealer.
A consensus of several dealers called a range of 4.4650-4.4750 rand per dollar for Friday.
In cross rate action, the rand was weaker against the German mark, costing 0.3782/3787 marks from 0.3798/3802 yesterday.
The local unit was changing hands at 25.8792/9190 yen from 25.5240/5480 previously and 7.3123/3217 rand to the British pound from 7.3433/3527 before.
On the bond market the key R150 bond was hobbled early by U.S. Treasury weakness and talk the Reserve Bank was selling bonds.
Yields eventually settled down in a narrow range and began creeping lower in the late afternoon on some book-squaring action.
The benchmark R150 bond was last at 15.020 percent from previous 14.910 percent.

Assisting some of the late retracement was talk that the South African Reserve Bank had finished selling bonds as part of its strategy to offset liquidity added by the part-privatisation of telecommunications utility Telkom.
South Africa's money market shortage was barely changed on Wednesday, edging down to 6.453 billion from 6.658 billion rand on Tuesday, the Reserve Bank said on Thursday.
Recent stability in the shortage caused rates at the longer end of the NCD curve to move lower on Thursday, money market players said.
Three-month NCD rates remained unchanged from Wednesday at 16.35 percent offered but 90-day BA rates shifted to 15.85 percent from 15.90 percent on Wednesday.
Foreigners were net buyers of 742.38 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Wednesday after selling 38.79 million rand on Tuesday, the Bond Exchange said.
Some debt market dealers said a large asset swap might have been behind the jump in offshore purchases.
Nominal Bond Exchange turnover rose to 7.62 billion rand on Wednesday from 5.47 billion rand on Tuesday.
